_comment: Zephyr's own kernel test suites, and how each one currently does on
wasm_node. scripts/check_kernel.py runs them and compares.
The point is that the kernel's evidence stops being one suite taken
once. A suite that does better than recorded is the interesting
direction and should be written down: check_kernel.py --update.
fails           the suite finished and some cases failed
does-not-finish the run ended without a verdict: a trap, a panic, or
note: why, when the cause is understood. An unexplained entry is an

suites.note: Passes since arch_busy_wait stopped replacing the kernel timer's alarm with its own: test_ms_time_duration's timer falls due during a busy-wait, and fires there now, as on hardware.
Passes since the busy-wait fix (see common): its duration and period checks busy-wait across timer expiries.

DEVICE_API_IS() does not recognise a child class. This is patch 0007's documented approximation, now demonstrated rather than predicted: wasm-ld cannot group a class section with its children's, so the end of the group is the end of the class's own section.
Passes since the busy-wait fix (see common). The slice was never late; the busy-wait that measured it hid the tick.

Traps on the first case. The thread entries take two parameters and are cast to k_thread_entry_t, which takes three; wasm type-checks indirect calls, so the call traps where every other target tolerates it. Correcting the signatures locally makes all 11 pass. Not a port bug and not fixable in the port. The fix is in upstream/zephyr/; with it applied (scripts/try_upstream.sh) the suite passes.

The same signature mismatch, reached through K_THREAD_DEFINE with an entry declared void f(void) rather than through an explicit cast. The fix is in upstream/zephyr/; with it applied (scripts/try_upstream.sh) the suite passes.
Passes since z_wasm_fatal_error may return: an essential thread that aborts itself panics after it is already dead, and the kernel switches away only once the fatal path returns.
Passes since the busy-wait fix (see common): test_time_slicing_preemptible busy-waits through each slice, and a slice that ended inside the wait was taken only after it.

Passes since iterable sections are laid out in upstream's order, which makes ztest run the cases in upstream's order too. In link order it panicked at test_k_heap_alloc_size[sizes/0] on ASSERTION FAIL [z_spin_lock_valid(l)]: some case that ran earlier left the heap's spinlock recorded as held. Which one was never found, so that is still unexplained; it no longer runs first. The timeout hypothesis was ruled out.

Upstream's kernel.common.stack_sentinel entry. Its first two cases raise a CPU exception by calling an illegal address and dividing by zero, and in wasm both are traps, which unwind to the host and cannot be caught. With those two raised in software instead (a scratch copy, not committed), every other case passes, both stack sentinel checks among them: from a timer interrupt and from a swap.
